Consider a directed weighted graph G(V, E), where V is the set of vertices and E is the set of edges. Suppose we use adjacency list to implement the graph. Consider a sequence of |V| operations with each corresponding to a different vertex in V. For the operation for vertex v, the cost is assumed to be the number of outgoing edges from v.  (a) What is the cost of the worst possible single operation in this sequence of operations? (b) What is the average amortized cost of the above sequence of operations based on aggregate analysis?

message.content:
The cost of an operation for vertex \(v\) is exactly the number of outgoing edges from \(v\), so the worst single operation in the sequence is determined by the vertex with the largest out-degree. In the worst case that out-degree can be as large as \(|E|\), or at most \(|V|-1\) if the graph is simple and has no self-loops.

* (a) The worst possible single operation has cost \(\max_{v\in V} \text{outdeg}(v)\), with an upper bound of \(|E|\) (or \(|V|-1\) for a simple directed graph without parallel edges and self-loops).
* (b) The total cost over the \(|V|\) operations is \(\sum_{v\in V} \text{outdeg}(v) = |E|\), so the average amortized cost is \(|E|/|V|\).
